topic: Passport Is Not Proof of Citizenship

subtopics.title: Identity Documents vs Citizenship
subtopics.summary: No single universal document conclusively proves Indian citizenship. Aadhaar shows identity and residence, a Voter ID shows electoral eligibility, and a Ration Card shows residence and welfare eligibility. Inclusion in the electoral roll creates a presumption of citizenship that only due legal process can displace.
facts: No single universal document conclusively proves Indian citizenship
Aadhaar: proof of identity and residence, not citizenship
Voter ID: establishes electoral eligibility, not citizenship
Ration Card: indicates residence and eligibility for welfare benefits, not citizenship
Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995): inclusion in electoral roll creates a presumption of citizenship
That presumption can be displaced only through due legal process
Citizenship Certificate is issued only to persons acquiring citizenship through registration or naturalisation
Persons acquiring citizenship by birth or descent do not receive a Citizenship Certificate
Sarbananda Sonowal vs Union of India (2005): burden of proving Indian citizenship lies on the person claiming it
Deletion from electoral roll does not amount to loss of citizenship

subtopics.title: Assam Accord and NRC
subtopics.summary: The Assam agitation of 1979-1985, led by AASU and AAGSP against illegal immigration, ended with a Memorandum of Settlement signed on August 15, 1985. Clause 6 of the Assam Accord mandates safeguards for Assamese identity. A committee headed by Justice (Retd) Biplab Kumar Sarma made 67 recommendations, of which 57 have been approved by the Assam Cabinet.
facts: Assam agitation years: 1979-1985
Agitation led by AASU and AAGSP against illegal immigration
Tripartite Memorandum of Settlement signed on August 15, 1985 by Central Government, Assam Government and agitation leaders
Clause 6 of Assam Accord: constitutional, legislative and administrative safeguards for Assamese identity and heritage
Committee headed by Justice (Retd) Biplab Kumar Sarma submitted 67 recommendations
57 recommendations approved by Assam Cabinet; 10 remain under discussion with Centre
AASU stands for All Assam Students' Union; AAGSP stands for All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad
Assam NRC: applicants had to establish links with legacy records predating 24 March 1971
NRC in Assam commenced in 2003 following an SC Order
NRC in Assam: 1951
